notes.summary: Native242's exact-original preservation claim fails. All 55 supplied bindings match; whole decoded controller/native inputs and grants coincide, while all six actual/expanded note texts differ.
notes.detailedSummary: An independent inert audit reconstructs native242's saved 21927-byte augmented task, matching its old inventory and task hash but differing from the exact 17550-byte original. This corrects actual/expanded notes n1 and n6 without affecting their mathematical arguments. Twenty-three saved own entries are checkable and match; eight unavailable artifacts and historical provider/build attestations remain unverified.
notes.text:
This is an independent documentary finding, not a mathematical theorem. All 55 supplied records—14 mathematical, 23 primary and 18 historical evidence—match their manifest byte counts and SHA-256 values. The historical controller/native inputs decode to equal WHOLE objects despite different bytes. Their entire imported G331 object and the current supplied G331 object equal the bound qualified grant. The six actual native242 FINAL notes and six expanded notes have equal IDs, supports and candidate flags but unequal summaries, detailed summaries and texts. Each expanded text occurs exactly in the complete argument.md. Actual FINAL text byte counts are 4015, 4884, 5390, 3798, 6003 and 5218; expanded counts are 7024, 8006, 7659, 5810, 9034 and 6590. These bodies were judged separately.

A documentary preservation assertion is FALSE. The exact original task has 17550 bytes and SHA-256 d524b816c1462a6909a85bd0e39b84ab34ca04be27ec99eccbfde7ffcc0316a8. Native242's saved own inventory identifies its original-task.json as 21927 bytes with SHA-256 370ab1eb8319a773be4e7df91270e48e235ff16930fed4e961f0b00eea2ef2e7. Fresh serialization of the decoded WHOLE historical controller task reproduces those 21927 bytes and that hash exactly. The historical freeze identifies that hash as task_sha256, separately from original_task_sha256. The augmented task contains the full original problem as a prefix, followed by the research assignment, and appends a deliverable sentence to the completion criteria. Thus the original family and criteria survive, but the saved object is not the unchanged original. This corrects actual/expanded n1 and n6 and the paper's preservation assertions without altering either author source. It does not change an envelope proof or make candidate=false dishonest.

Our original-task.json is the exact 17550-byte original, copied unchanged. The augmented reconstruction remains separately in review-data/native242-reconstructed-saved-original-task.json. Actual and expanded notes are separately decoded under review-data/. Of 31 saved own inventory entries, 23 can be verified against supplied bytes or exact reconstructions, including all six expanded texts; eight cannot: the old PDF, audit/build/final-audit/delimiter-repair scripts, annotation render and two build transcripts. The saved 36-input inventory reports all matches, and its 23 primary records agree with the current exact primary inventory. Unavailable historical mathematical paths were not followed. Old build.json records two exit-zero pdflatex invocations; final-audit.json marks 25 checks true, including original_task_unchanged. That check compared the augmented assigned task rather than the exact original. These records establish what was reported, not the missing PDF/build output or provider identity.

Only unchanged qualified G331 is a supplied correctness/source grant. Its entire object, mandatory annotation, source ledger and exact scope remain attached unchanged. We use its independent actual primary-model Cartier-degree cone, C_geom=C_ideal, D_geom=D_ideal, all-support boundary, exact positive C/D conductor descent, normal-domain divisorial density and fixed-divisorial inequality, and exact smooth BFJ comparison. notes.summary: Proved full raw-C/raw-D equality, regularization positivity iff raw continuity, an exact ideal formula and primary-gauge covariance for the unchanged cone.
notes.detailedSummary: Compact common-index covers and finite-max approximation prove the raw envelope criterion. P(p*)=p proves positivity of regularization precisely when the raw output is continuous. Actual primary/unit ideals J_k give the full rational and factorial supremum; no increasing-limit membership follows. Identical ideal constraints and bounded-denominator upper limits establish gauge covariance.
notes.text:
Fix G331's unchanged cone and retain every support. Let X=V_a(R) be a nonempty compact primary section, Q the finite nonnegative real sums of negative unit-or-primary ideal gauges, C its uniform closure in finite continuous functions, and D infima of actual nonempty decreasing C-nets, including bottom. C contains negative constants and is stable under finite maxima. D is nonpositive and upper semicontinuous because {inf_i g_i<t}=union_i{g_i<t}. Finite maxima in D are legitimate: on the product directed set, max(g_i,h_j) decreases to max(inf_i g_i,inf_j h_j), since simultaneous finite strict upper tests can be met. Subtracting a nonnegative constant preserves both classes. Empty sections have their unique empty function.

For a finite continuous obstacle phi, let p=P_D phi be the supremum of all D-minorants. Negative constants bound it below and min(phi,0) bounds it above. If u=inf_i g_i<=phi and epsilon>0, the open sets {g_i<phi+epsilon} cover X. Directedness and a finite subcover select one common term. Then g_i-epsilon is a C-minorant and is at least u-epsilon. Taking suprema and sending epsilon to zero proves P_D phi=P_C phi. The common finite bounded p is lower semicontinuous.

If a finite continuous u belongs to D, the same compact-cover argument with g_i<u+epsilon proves uniform convergence and u in C. If p is continuous, the open sets {g>p-epsilon}, over all C-minorants, cover X. The maximum from a finite subcover lies between p-epsilon and p; uniform closedness puts p in C. Consequently p in D iff p is continuous iff p in C, equivalently iff a greatest D-minorant exists. Monotonicity, positive homogeneity and clipping the obstacle against zero follow directly. Shifting competitors down proves ||P phi-P psi||_infinity<=||phi-psi||_infinity. No increasing completion principle is used.

Define p*(x)=inf_{open U containing x}sup_U p. For bounded p this is upper semicontinuous: if p*(x)<t, some U has sup_U p<t and the same bound works throughout U. Since phi is continuous and p<=phi, p*<=phi. Every original D-minorant is below p*, and every D-minorant of p* is below phi. Hence P_D(p*)=p. If p* belongs to D, it is itself a competitor, forcing p*<=p and thus equality. As p is also lsc, it is continuous. Conversely continuous p equals p* and belongs to C. Therefore p* in D iff p continuous iff p in C iff p*=p. This verifies ROOT335's regularization criterion independently.

An exact ideal construction works in every primary gauge. For k>=1 define J_k={f in R: v(f)>=-k phi(v) for every v in X}. It is an ideal by the semivaluation axioms and nonnegativity on R. If M>=max(0,-min phi) and integer L>=kM, then a^L is contained in J_k. If phi is negative somewhere, units are excluded and J_k is proper maximal-primary; otherwise J_k=R. Finite generation gives a_k=-v(J_k)/k<=phi, and a_k belongs to Q with the unit convention zero. Every rational single profile -v(I)/k<=phi has I contained in J_k, hence is at most a_k.

Single rational profiles are uniformly dense in C: rationally approximate the finitely many real coefficients of a Q sum, synchronize denominators and take a product ideal. Given a C-minorant g and epsilon>0, approximate it with error less than epsilon/4 by q=-v(I)/k. Subtract a rational delta between epsilon/4 and epsilon/2. Because v(a)=1, common denominators and a boundary-ideal power realize q-delta as a single rational primary profile still below phi and within epsilon of g. Thus p=sup_k a_k. The defining inequalities give J_k J_l contained in J_{k+l} and J_k^l contained in J_{kl}; consequently a_{n!} increases and has supremum p, since every fixed k eventually divides n!. This is a raw formula and does not imply that its increasing limit belongs to D.

For another primary ideal b put d(v)=v(b), H_ab(v)=v/d(v), and T_ab f(H_ab v)=f(v)/d(v). G331 supplies the homeomorphism H_ab and order bijections on C,D, with d and 1/d bounded positive continuous. Transform obstacles by the same rule. Bijection of competitors proves P_b(T_ab phi)=T_ab(P_a phi), including extended obstacles. Multiplying the J_k constraint by d proves that J_k is literally unchanged. Composing transformations telescopes the second denominator v(c)/v(b), giving division by v(c) and the exact three-gauge cocycle. For bounded p, near x the difference |p(y)/d(y)-p(y)/d(x)| is bounded by ||p|| times |1/d(y)-1/d(x)| and tends uniformly to zero. Neighborhood upper limits therefore give (T_ab p)*=T_ab(p*). No infinite conductor value is divided out.

These are mathematical proofs relative to G331, reconstructing actual242 n1, the gauge portion of n5 and ROOT335 sections6–7. Full artifacts: n2.md, whole-proof.md and P12.3-conductor-criterion-paper.tex. Rerun documentary/static checks: python review_audit.py; python finalize_review.py. Compilation is reserved to ROOT; execution and bindings do not establish these proofs.

notes.summary: Native242's strictly negative double-plane counterexample passes independently: exact full-family envelope, no maximal minorant and nonpositive regularization.
notes.detailedSummary: Actual primary-ideal tuples descend positively before use. A universal second-branch order inequality bounds every completed geometric competitor; the sequence attains the exact pointwise bounds on all supports. The identified nonminimal conductor point causes failure of USC, and finite maxima strictly improve every admissible minorant. ROOT335 supplies no premise or repair.
notes.text:
Independent mathematical judgment on actual242 n2, its expanded version and paper section2: PASS at the stated algebraically closed characteristic-zero scope. Set R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy), A=k[x,z]_(x,z), B=k[y,z]_(y,z), T=k[z]_(z). The local fibre product R=A times_T B is exact: polynomial pairs with common residue h are represented by f+g-h. For denominators u in A and v in B, the pair (u v(0,z),v u(0,z)) has equal unit residues and clears both denominators by a downstairs unit. S=A times B is finite, generated by its two idempotents, normal and birational componentwise. Its conductor is (x)A times(y)B=(x,y)R, as multiplication by the idempotents tests.

The entire boundary is the union of its two closed branch images: xy=0 forces v(x)=infinity or v(y)=infinity. They intersect only at q, killing x,y and giving z value one, the unique centered normalized semivaluation on the quotient DVR T. Upstairs denote its representatives q_A,q_B. All other normalization fibres are singleton, directly from this description or G331's finite-conductor rule. The nonminimal support (x,y) at q is essential.

Define phi_A=-1 and phi_B=-3+min(w(y),2). Truncated evaluation is continuous, including at infinity, and both identified values equal -1. Compact quotient descent gives a finite continuous phi in [-2,-1] on the entire boundary. On B, maximal-ideal order o_B satisfies w(f)>=o_B(f): membership in (y,z)^d gives value at least d because w(y),w(z)>=1; units have value zero. Therefore every negative primary profile satisfies g(w)<=g(o_B). Uniform closure and then actual decreasing infima preserve this inequality in C and D. Every D-minorant of phi is thus <=-2 throughout B, because phi(o_B)=-2.

For n>=1 the proper primary ideal J_n=(x^n,xz^(n-1),z^(2n)) on A gives u_n,A=-w(J_n)/n, paired with u_n,B=-2. Both are in C before use. They agree at q_A,q_B, so G331's positive C descent puts u_n in C_R. They are admissible. Write a=w(x), b=w(z), min(a,b)=1. The value is -min(a,(a+(n-1)b)/n,2b), with the n=1 middle monomial evaluated as x when b=infinity. If a<=b, then a=1 and the value is -1. If a>b is finite, b=1 and min(a,1+(a-1)/n,2) decreases to one. If a=infinity, the point is q_A and the minimum remains two. This exhausts all supports; cancellation is irrelevant because the actual generators are monomials.

Hence the exact full-family raw envelope p is -1 on A minus q_A and -2 at q and throughout B. The obstacle and universal B inequality give these upper bounds for EVERY D competitor; the already positive u_n attain the matching lower bounds as a pointwise supremum. Their increasing character is not used to infer membership. Monomial valuations w_L(x)=L,w_L(z)=1 converge to q_A on every localized polynomial: positive x-degree terms acquire values tending to infinity, the residue modulo x has its z order, and unit denominators have zero value. Thus p(w_L)=-1 but p(q)=-2. It is not USC and is not in D.

No minorant is maximal. For u<=phi in D, u(q)<=-2, so USC gives a neighborhood where u<-3/2. Choose finite L>=2 mapping into that neighborhood and n>2(L-1). Then u_n(w_L)=-1-(L-1)/n>-3/2. The finite maximum max(u,u_n) remains a D-minorant and strictly improves u. Regularization p* equals p off q because the branch images are closed, and equals -1 at q by the same sequence and global bound. Although p*<=phi, its B values -1 at q_B and -2 at o_B violate the universal order inequality; p* is not geometric.

This reconstructs the entire positive-minorant, exact-envelope, no-maximality and regularization dependency chain. Every geometric membership precedes competitor use. It also verifies the normalization example in actual242 n5. No later ROOT335 result was used to accept or repair native242. No sampled valuation experiment replaces this all-support proof.

notes.summary: Native242's smooth, extended-USC and curve theorems pass at exact hypotheses; ROOT335's smooth uniform estimate also passes.
notes.detailedSummary: BFJ's determining-envelope estimate, closed-simplex continuity and canonical retractions produce uniform positive primary approximation on all supports. PA density handles every continuous obstacle only in the published smooth characteristic-zero range. One actual decreasing C-envelope net treats extended USC obstacles when continuity is established. Positive normalization descent and DVR product classes prove all excellent reduced-curve clipping.
notes.text:
Independent mathematical judgments on actual242 n3–n5, their expanded bodies and ROOT335 section11: PASS at their stated domains. The sole new essential primary publication is Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson, Valuations and plurisubharmonic singularities, Publ. RIMS44 (2008),449–494. We freshly read the exact bound text's complete Setting, divisor/semivaluation conventions, simple-modification retractions and 1.13–1.15 including proofs, 2.1 and 2.5–2.8, 3.11 including its immediate proof, and the entire Section3.5, including 3.15–3.18, Lemma3.22 and the complete remainder of3.18. Exact ranges and hashes are in whole-source-application-ledger.md. The application is ONLY at a smooth affine closed germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, dimension>=2. Historical Hironaka/principalization, DEL multiplier subadditivity, Izumi/ELS and graded-family inputs are disclosed ordinary published background, not recursively reread or transferred to singular/arbitrary-characteristic settings.

Initially use the maximal-ideal gauge. Let f be finite continuous and determined on one BFJ dual complex. Choose M>=1 with f>=-M. The coefficient supremum W of nef Z<=Z(f) is genuinely weak-nef: replace candidates by max(Z,-M), direct finite maxima and take their bounded coefficientwise limit. BFJ's weak cone is closed and finite-max stable by2.1. This is the published smooth coefficient operation, not increasing closure of singular D. BFJ3.11 gives H_W continuous on every CLOSED simplex, with canonical extension H(v)=inf_pi H(r_pi v). Rational divisorial density and substantive closed-simplex continuity extend coefficient bounds; the canonical infimum then gives -M<=H<=0 on all supports. On the determining complex H<=f, and2.7 gives H(v)<=H(r_pi v)<=f(r_pi v)=f(v). For every nonbottom D-minorant u, G331's precise BFJ comparison gives nef coefficients Z(u)<=Z(f), hence <=W. Closed-simplex continuity and all retractions imply u<=H. Bottom is harmless.

If W=0, H=0 belongs to C. Otherwise BFJ3.18(iii) gives c>0 and W_k<=W<=(1-c/k)W_{k-c}, with W_t=t^(-1)Z(L_infinity(tW)), for real k>c. The required hypothesis is met: W is the envelope of determining data. Each L_infinity(tW) contains completed m^ceil(tM), and is proper since nonzero W has a negative coefficient whereas units have coefficient zero. For integer t>=1 contract this primary ideal to I_t in R by G331's exact completion/primary contraction. Its all-support profile f_t=-v(I_t)/t lies in C and satisfies -M-1/t<=f_t<=0. Taking k=t+c and extending coefficient inequalities through closed simplices and canonical infima gives f_t<=H<=t/(t+c)f_t. Consequently 0<=H-f_t<=c/(t+c)(M+1/t), uniformly on the entire section, and H belongs to C before geometric interpretation. The stronger ROOT335 estimate also follows: multiplication of the upper inequality gives f_t>=(1+c/t)H, so 0<=H-f_t<=-(c/t)H<=cM/t. Signs are correct because H<=0. The constant comes from one fixed determining complex; no whole-boundary thinness bound is asserted. The complete published proof uses3.22, smooth multiplier subadditivity and bounded thinness against strict negativity on that complex. Its actual hypotheses are met.

BFJ1.15 proves uniform density of PA obstacles, each determined on one complex. The proved raw contraction in n2 makes their C-envelopes converge uniformly to P phi for every finite continuous obstacle. Uniform closedness gives P phi in C, admissible and greatest. This establishes both drafts' ALL-continuous-obstacle result on all supports only in the exact published smooth range. Gauge transport is n2; no singular all-model cofinality is used.

For bounded-above extended USC phi:X->[−infinity,M], assume the continuous-envelope property separately. Compact Hausdorff normality gives the required cutoffs: finite Hausdorff separation covers of disjoint compact closed sets yield normality; shrinking neighborhoods and recursively separating at dyadic rationals produce open O_r with closure(O_r) contained in O_s for r<s. The function inf{r:x in O_r}, with endpoint conventions, is continuous because strict sublevel and superlevel sets are unions of O_r and complements of closures. Thus for finite phi(x)<ell<t, including bottom at x, choose continuous chi with chi(x)=1 and closed support inside {phi<ell}. For M'>max(M,ell), F=chi ell+(1-chi)M' strictly exceeds phi everywhere and F(x)=ell<t. All finite continuous strict majorants form a nonempty minimum-closed downward-directed net with infimum phi. Their ALREADY positive C-envelopes decrease. The infimum belongs to D by its actual definition, is below phi and dominates every D-minorant of phi. This proves actual242 n4 without flattening nested D nets. The same argument applies to any decreasing continuous obstacle net whose envelopes are established in C. Extended output regularity is USC; no general continuity assertion follows.

For arbitrary obstacles, G331's positive normalization descent identifies exactly the downstairs admissible family with full-fibre-constant upstairs D-minorants. Pointwise supremum gives the constrained identity. A fibre-constant obstacle does not erase that constraint. If an unconstrained upstairs greatest envelope is separately in D and fibre-constant, its positive descent is the downstairs envelope. If the boundary map is bijective, it is a compact homeomorphism; separately good normal centres therefore give C-envelopes, then the preceding USC extension. Primary or unit conductor is sufficient for this bijectivity, not a necessary classification.

For every excellent reduced local curve, finite normalization has finitely many DVR local centres. Every nonmaximal localization is a generic field, on which normalization is an isomorphism. The finite module S/R is supported only at the maximal ideal and is killed by a maximal-ideal power; conductor is primary or unit, with finite value everywhere. Hence the boundary map is a homeomorphism. Each DVR section is the singleton ord_i/ord_i(a), and C consists of every finite nonpositive constant, realized by a nonnegative real multiple of the parameter-ideal profile, zero by the unit. Granted semilocal product/gluing and positive C descent give C_R=(−infinity,0]^r. Already positive finite tuples max(h_i,-N) decrease to every extended nonpositive tuple, yielding D_R=[−infinity,0]^r. Only after this membership proof does min(phi_i,0) give the greatest geometric envelope for EVERY extended branch obstacle. Positive gauge factors ord_i(a)/ord_i(b) commute with clipping. Mixed zero, partial bottom, all bottom and all zero remain. Branches are local normalization centres, not minimal primes. Nilpotents are reduced away; dimension zero has the unique empty function. This is geometric comparison through G331, not literal radial identification or an ideal cone renamed.

notes.summary: ROOT335's separate all-characteristic explicit double-plane obstruction passes over the full geometric competitor family.
notes.detailedSummary: The actual downstairs ideal sequence (x^N,y,z^N) and continuous obstacle −1/(1+v(x)) give raw envelope −1/2 on the first branch and zero on the second away from the conductor point. Regularization violates the primary-order inequality, and no maximal minorant exists. This later construction is additional content, not a premise for native242.
notes.text:
Independent reconstruction of ROOT335 sections1–5 and7–8, separately from native242: PASS. For ANY field k use R=(k[x,y,z]/xy)_(x,y,z). The exact fibre-product, finite normalization and conductor arguments in n3 use polynomial arithmetic and unit denominators and require no characteristic or algebraic-closure assumption. Its closed branch images X1, where y is killed, and X2, where x is killed, meet only at c, killing x,y and giving z value one. On X1, maximal-ideal order o1 gives h(w)<=h(o1) for every h in D_R through negative primary profiles, uniform closure and actual decreasing infima. That order argument is valid over any field and every support.

The downstairs obstacle phi(v)=-1/(1+v(x)), with value zero at infinity, is finite continuous in [-1/2,0]. It is zero on X2 and at c, and equals -1/2 at o1. The actual proper primary downstairs ideals I_N=(x^N,y,z^N) give h_N=-v(I_N)/(2N) in Q_R. Their negative exceptional Cartier presentations on actual primary blowups are geometric through G331's core inclusion; no positivity descent shortcut is required. On X1 they equal -1/2. On X2 they equal -(1/2)min(v(y)/N,v(z)); at c they equal -1/2, while elsewhere v(y) is finite and they increase to zero. Infinite v(z), other supports and cancellation are included, since actual monomial generator values determine the ideal. These functions lie below phi.

EVERY D competitor is at most -1/2 throughout X1 by its value at o1 and at most zero on X2 by the obstacle. The h_N match these full-family upper bounds pointwise. Thus the exact raw envelope p is -1/2 on all X1, including c, and zero on X2 minus c. Monomial valuations v(y)=L,v(z)=1 on X2 converge to c on every localized polynomial. Hence p is not USC. Its regularization is -1/2 on X1 minus c and zero on all X2, still below phi; it violates h(c)<=h(o1) and is not geometric. There is also no maximal minorant: every competitor has value<=-1/2 at c, USC makes it <-1/4 nearby, and one nearby finite-L point followed by sufficiently large N has h_N>-1/4 there. Their finite maximum strictly improves that competitor. The separated normal envelopes are constants -1/2 and zero, so fail the shared conductor fibre condition even though both are continuous and geometric.

This differs from native242's STRICTLY NEGATIVE obstacle and J_n tuple sequence, verified by their own proof in n3. The simpler later all-characteristic construction is additional content, not acceptance premise or repair. General raw/regularization equivalences, exact J_k formula and gauge covariance were independently proved in n2; reduced-curve clipping is n4. No increasing D membership is inferred from the displayed sequence. Every semivaluation support and the identified nonminimal conductor point remain.

notes.summary: Both directions of ROOT335's exact conductor criterion pass, including primary masks, dense finite-conductor equality and the obstruction from different normal centres.
notes.detailedSummary: For every excellent reduced local germ and finite continuous obstacle, downstairs regularization is in D exactly when the separated raw normal envelope is continuous and constant on every full fibre. Actual primary conductor masks descend positively before raw limits; density is a qualified G331 conclusion. Fixed normal nonunit bounds yield a downstairs counterexample whenever a fibre joins different normal centres. General normal continuity and internal-fibre classification remain unresolved.
notes.text:
Independent reconstruction of ROOT335 sections9–10: PASS, using only qualified G331 and the compact-envelope arguments proved in n2. Let R be excellent reduced local of positive dimension, S its finite normalization, X its a-primary section, and Y the finite disjoint union of ALL local normal-centre sections for aS. Retain every support and restriction fibre rho:Y->X. Let c be conductor, U={v(c)<infinity}, U_S=rho^(-1)U. G331 supplies surjectivity and singleton fibres over U. A regular conductor element exists and is nonzero on every component. Every fraction-field centred divisorial point has finite conductor value. G331's proved divisorial density on all-support excellent normal-domain sections therefore makes U_S dense on EVERY normal centre. Empty zero-dimensional sections contribute no point. No resolution or singular multiplier theorem is used.

For a finite continuous phi let p_R,p_S be full raw D-envelopes downstairs and upstairs of phi,rho*phi. N2 applies to the finite semilocal product class: both equal C-suprema and are finite lsc. Pullback of competitors gives rho*p_R<=p_S. Fix ANY C_S minorant g of rho*phi and choose M>=0 such that -M<=g and -M<=rho*phi everywhere. For N>=1 use the ACTUAL DOWNSTAIRS primary-or-unit ideal c+a^N and mask b_N(w)=-(M/N)w((c+a^N)S)=-M min(w(c)/N,1). Only finite ideal values occur, including when w(c)=infinity, so M=0 is harmless. Define g_N=max(g+b_N,-M). Sum/max closure puts it in C_S, and both entries lie below rho*phi. On the whole infinite-conductor stratum g_N=-M because g<=0. Elsewhere all full fibres are singletons. Thus g_N is constant on EVERY fibre; G331's POSITIVE C descent gives h_N in C_R with rho*h_N=g_N and h_N<=phi. For w in U_S the mask tends to zero and g_N(w)->g(w). Therefore rho*p_R(w)>=g(w). Taking the supremum of ALL C_S competitors and using n2 gives rho*p_R=p_S on U_S. This is raw equality proved by already positive approximants, not increasing-limit membership.

The exact criterion is p_R* in D_R iff p_S is continuous AND constant on every rho-fibre. If p_R* belongs to D_R, n2 makes p_R continuous in C_R. Its continuous pullback u equals p_S on dense U_S and is <=p_S globally. For any w choose a net w_i in U_S tending to w. Lower semicontinuity gives p_S(w)<=liminf p_S(w_i)=u(w), proving equality on ALL Y. Thus p_S is continuous and fibre-constant. Conversely, continuous p_S belongs to C_S by n2's finite-maximum approximation. Full fibre constancy and positive descent give h in C_R with rho*h=p_S. It is below phi, so h<=p_R; the general pullback inequality and surjectivity give p_R<=h. Hence p_R=h in C_R and p_R*=p_R. Both directions are proved without a normal-centre envelope theorem. When that continuous-envelope property is separately known, fibre constancy is the sole remaining test. If rho is bijective, it is a homeomorphism and the universal continuous-envelope property is equivalent to that of its normal centres through G331's bidirectional class identification.

Suppose now a fibre joins w_A,w_B on DIFFERENT positive-dimensional normal local centres A,B. Choose a centred normalized divisorial nu_A on A. It has finite conductor value, so its image x_A has singleton full fibre and lies outside the closed union F of images of all other centres.
